verdict.reasoning: Patient reports decreased hearing in the left ear: “I just feel like I can't really hear as well as I used to…”, localized to left ear: “Just the left ear, yeah”, and duration: “For about six weeks.”

Patient describes intermittent tinnitus in the left ear triggered by TV or music: “I occasionally get like a ringing in my left ear… It’s kind of on and off… if I'm watching TV or listening to music or something. Something that will set off the ringing in the ear.”

Transcript: “there's actually been a few times when I felt kind of a bit sick or a bit dizzy as well… just a little bit kind of off balance.” Patient explicitly says it is “not that kind of dizziness you get with nausea,” so associating the dizziness with mild nausea is not supported and partially contradicts the clarification.

Doctor asks about ear symptoms and fever/itch: “have you had any pain from the ear at all? Okay. Any discharge coming out of the ear? Okay. Have you been experiencing any fever?... And has your ear been itchy at all?” Patient responds “Not specifically, apart from the dizziness and sickness I mentioned before” to fever and “No” to itching, implying denial of pain, discharge, fever, and itch.
Doctor: “Have you any chest pain with it?… Any palpitations? Heartbeat and fast.” Patient answers “No.” This supports denial of chest pain and palpitations.

Patient: “I had something maybe about a year ago, but it only lasted a couple of days. It wasn't anything as long as this.” This describes a remote, similar, self-resolving episode lasting days about a year ago.
Doctor: “do you use cotton wool buds to try and clean out wax from your ears?” Patient: “No. I don't know.” This supports that the patient does not use cotton buds for cleaning ears.

The consultation is clearly via video/remote (“before we start your appointment…”, “you can speak to her and we'll serve a video”), and there is no mention of any physical examination being performed; instead, they plan a future in-person exam, supporting that no physical exam was done in this encounter.

Clinician summarizes: “you've had ringing, difficulty hearing in your left ear and feeling slightly sick… and that's been… for the six weeks.” This reflects assessment of unilateral left-sided hearing loss for 6 weeks with intermittent tinnitus and dizziness/sick feeling.

Doctor: “Simple things might be wax. Someone might have impacted wax blocking the tube going into the eardrum, which can lead to muffled hearing… we need to exclude that first.” This shows the clinician is considering ear wax impaction as a possible cause.

Doctor discusses tinnitus and balance system: “Does it seem like the ringing that you've got that you've got something called tinnitus… It might be that there's a problem inside the drum or the balance system within the ear.” This indicates consideration of tinnitus and a vestibular/balance disorder as otologic etiologies.

Doctor: “book you in for a face to face appointment in one of our clinics… within the next four, five days or so… one of the GP will just have a quick look down the ear, figure out whether there's a physical blockage or whether there's something else going on.” This is a plan for in-person review with otoscopy/ear exam.

Doctor: “I'm going to paste the link for a leaflet about tinnitus in the notes for this appointment. I'd really appreciate it if you could start reading about it.” This matches providing a tinnitus information leaflet.

Doctor: “If there's any problem, any issues between now and when the clinic appointment is, just book another appointment…” This is equivalent to advising the patient to rebook if symptoms worsen or problems arise.

Doctor: “I'll send a message to our admin team, I'll ask them to slot you into one of our clinics… I'll leave the number in the notes of this appointment, ring them, and then they'll stop you in.” This shows admin staff will arrange the appointment and a contact number will be provided.
Doctor: “what we'll do is we'll see you in about four or five days time…”, confirming follow-up face-to-face review within 4–5 days.
